name: Nigerian Beef Stew over Rice
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cut the chuck roast into chunks and boil it with some of the onion, the bay leaves, thyme, curry powder, and salt until just tender. Strain and keep the stock.
Blend the diced tomatoes with the bell peppers, jalapeno, remaining onion, garlic, and ginger until smooth.
Heat the vegetable oil and olive oil in a wide pot and pour in the blended base. Fry it, stirring, until it thickens noticeably and the raw edge cooks off.
Stir in the tomato paste and keep frying a few more minutes so the paste loses its metallic taste.
Add the boiled beef, the reserved stock, and the beef broth. Simmer uncovered 30 to 40 minutes until the sauce is thick enough to sit on a spoon.
Taste and correct the salt and pepper. The stew should taste sharper than you think, because the rice will mute it.
Cook the rice separately and keep it plain.
head_steps: Boil the cubed beef with onion, bay, thyme, and curry powder, then reserve the stock.
Blend tomatoes, bell peppers, jalapeno, onion, garlic, and ginger smooth.
Fry the blended base in oil until thick, then fry in the tomato paste.
Add the beef, reserved stock, and broth and simmer 30 to 40 minutes.
Cook the rice and portion stew and rice into 14 containers.

findings.detail: 0.12 cups (28 g) of chicken broth is costed (the source's bouillon-powder analog) but the steps use only the reserved beef stock and beef broth, never the chicken broth.

name: One-Pot Creamy Cajun Sausage Pasta
ingredients: Ziti Pasta (Great Value): 37.25 oz dry (1058 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Slice the smoked sausage into coins, dice the onion and red bell pepper, and mince the garlic.
Heat the olive oil in a large deep pot and brown the sausage coins until the edges take on color, then set them aside.
Cook the onion and pepper in the sausage fat until they soften, then add the garlic and the Cajun seasoning and stir for a minute so the spices bloom.
Pour in the chicken broth and the diced tomatoes and bring it to a boil, scraping the bottom clean.
Stir in the dry pasta, drop it to a simmer, and cook uncovered while stirring often so nothing sticks. The pasta will drink most of the liquid.
Whisk the cornstarch into a little cold water to make a slurry, then stir it into the pot and let it thicken for a minute.
Turn the heat low, return the sausage, and stir in the heavy cream and parmesan until the sauce goes smooth.
head_steps: Brown the sliced smoked sausage in olive oil and set it aside.
Cook the onion and red pepper in the fat, then add the garlic and Cajun seasoning.
Add the chicken broth and diced tomatoes and bring to a boil.
Stir in the dry pasta and simmer uncovered, stirring often, until tender.
Thicken with a cornstarch slurry, then return the sausage and stir in the cream and parmesan.

findings.detail: 1 tbsp salt and 0.5 tbsp pepper are costed but the steps never use them or say 'season' (the source relies on the Cajun seasoning and lists no salt/pepper).

name: Oyakodon (Japanese Chicken and Egg Rice Bowls)
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh (Member's Mark): 4.25 lb (1984 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the rice: 7 cups dry with water per your usual method.
In your big pot, combine the chicken broth, soy sauce, mirin, and sugar and bring to a simmer.
Add the chicken thighs cut into bite-size pieces and most of the green onions. Simmer 8 to 10 minutes until the chicken reads 165 F.
Beat the eggs lightly, just until streaky, not uniform.
Pour the eggs evenly over the simmering chicken, cover, and cook 2 to 3 minutes. For meal prep that reheats safely, cook the eggs fully set, not runny.
Spoon the chicken and egg mixture with plenty of broth over rice in each container and top with the remaining green onions.
head_steps: Cook the rice.
Simmer broth, soy sauce, mirin, and sugar, then add bite-size chicken thighs and green onions.
Cook 8 to 10 minutes until the chicken reaches 165 F.
Pour lightly beaten eggs over the top, cover, and cook until fully set.
Spoon chicken, egg, and broth over rice in 14 containers and top with green onions.

findings.detail: We cost 7 yellow onions but no step ever uses them; the source (justonecookbook.com) simmers the sliced onion in the soy-mirin broth as the first cooking step, so the onion should go into our step 3 simmer.

findings.ingredient: Salt (1 tbsp) and Black Pepper (0.5 tbsp)
findings.detail: Both are costed but no step uses them or says 'season'; the source seasons only with the dashi/soy/mirin/sugar sauce.

name: Pakistani Beef Kofta Curry
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.

Mix the ground beef with a small amount of finely grated onion, minced jalapeno, chopped cilantro, the flour, and the ground cumin, coriander, chili powder, and salt. Knead it until it is smooth and slightly sticky.
Roll the mixture into even meatballs and set them on a tray in the fridge while you build the gravy.
Slice the rest of the onions thin and fry them in the vegetable oil over medium heat, patiently, until they are deep golden brown. This step is the entire dish, so do not rush it.
Add the minced garlic and the turmeric and cook 1 minute, then take the pot off the heat for a moment.
Whisk the Greek yogurt smooth and stir it in off the heat so it does not split, then return the pot to low and cook until the oil starts to separate at the edges.
Lower the koftas into the gravy in a single layer, add a cup or so of water, cover, and simmer 25 to 30 minutes. Shake the pot instead of stirring so the meatballs hold together.
Finish with garam masala and the remaining cilantro, and cook the rice separately.
head_steps: Knead ground beef with grated onion, jalapeno, cilantro, flour, and spices and roll into koftas.
Fry the sliced onions in oil until deep golden, then add garlic and turmeric.
Whisk in the yogurt off the heat, then cook until the oil separates.
Lower in the koftas with a little water and simmer 25 to 30 minutes.
Finish with garam masala and cilantro, cook the rice, and portion into 14 containers.

findings.detail: Costed but no step uses it or says 'season'; step 2's kofta spice list (cumin, coriander, chili powder, salt) and step 8's garam masala never include black pepper.

name: Panang Chicken Curry
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh (Member's Mark): 2.5 lb (1135 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.

Soak the dried chiles in hot water for 20 minutes. Drain them and blend with the peanuts, lemongrass paste, ginger, garlic, ground coriander, salt and a splash of the soaking water into a thick, coarse paste.

Spoon the thick cream off the top of the unshaken coconut milk cans into your largest pot, reserving the thin liquid. Cook it with the vegetable oil over medium-high for 3 to 5 minutes until the oil splits out.
Add your panang paste and the diced onion and fry it in that oil for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring hard, until it darkens a shade and smells nutty and sharp at the same time.
Add the chicken thighs cut into strips and turn them in the paste for 3 minutes, then pour in the reserved coconut liquid and the chicken broth.
Simmer uncovered 20 to 25 minutes, letting the sauce reduce until it is genuinely thick. Panang is supposed to cling, not pool, so give it the time.
Season with the fish sauce and sugar, add the green beans, and cook 4 minutes until they are tender but still have snap.
Turn off the heat and stir in the fresh basil. Cook the rice separately, steam it covered 10 minutes, and fold it in or bed the curry on top of it.
head_steps: Soak the dried chiles, then blend with peanuts, lemongrass, ginger, garlic and coriander into a coarse paste.
Fry the thick coconut cream with oil until it splits, then fry the paste and onion 3 to 4 minutes.
Add the chicken, the reserved coconut liquid and the broth, and simmer uncovered 20 to 25 minutes until thick.
Season with fish sauce and sugar and add the green beans for 4 minutes.
Stir in the basil off the heat and portion into 14 containers with rice.

findings.detail: Costed but never used in any step; the paste, simmer, and 'season with the fish sauce and sugar' steps never mention pepper (salt is used in the paste).

name: Peruvian Tallarines Verdes con Carne (Green Spaghetti with Beef)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Thaw and squeeze the frozen chopped spinach as dry as you can get it. Water is the enemy of this sauce.
Heat the olive oil in a pan and cook the garlic gently until fragrant but not browned.
Blend the spinach, fresh basil, cooked garlic and its oil, walnuts, butter crackers, milk, ricotta cheese, and parmesan cheese until smooth and thick, then season with salt and black pepper.
Cook the rice according to the package to serve underneath.
Season the beef with salt and plenty of black pepper and sear it hard in a very hot pan, in batches, until browned outside and still pink within, then rest it and slice against the grain.
Warm the green sauce gently over low heat, stirring, and thin it with a splash of milk if it has tightened up. Do not boil it or the cheese will go grainy.
Taste and adjust the salt, since spinach and cheese sauces almost always need more than you expect.
head_steps: Thaw and squeeze the frozen spinach completely dry.
Cook the garlic gently in olive oil until fragrant.
Blend spinach, basil, garlic, walnuts, crackers, milk, ricotta, and parmesan into a thick sauce.
Cook the rice base.
Season and sear the beef hard in batches, rest, and slice against the grain.
Warm the sauce gently, season, and portion rice, sauce, and beef into 14 containers.

findings.detail: The dish IS green spaghetti (source tosses the sauce with cooked spaghetti), but our steps never boil the 49.5 oz of spaghetti we cost, and the warmed sauce is never combined with any pasta.
Step 5 says 'Cook the rice according to the package to serve underneath' but rice is nowhere in the costed ingredient list (the list buys spaghetti instead).

name: Ground Beef Philly Cheesesteak Bowls
steps: Brown the ground beef in a big skillet, breaking it up as it cooks, then drain off any grease.
Add the sliced mushrooms, green peppers, and onion and cook until they soften, about 6 to 8 minutes.
Stir in the minced garlic and a splash of beef broth, then let it simmer a couple minutes to pull it all together.
Kill the heat and lay the provolone over the top so it melts into the beef.
Spoon it over cooked white rice and stir once so every bite gets some cheese.

name: Salisbury Steak and Potato Bowls
ingredients: Worcestershire Sauce (Lea & Perrins): 1 tsp (patties) + 1/2 tsp (gravy) (25 g)
Black Pepper (Great Value): to taste (4 g)
steps: Mix the ground beef with the bread crumbs and shape into patties.
Brown the patties in a large skillet, then set them aside.
Cook the sliced mushrooms and onions in the same pan until soft.
Stir in the beef broth and tomato paste and let it simmer into a gravy, then return the patties to the pan.
Roast or boil the potatoes until fork tender.
Serve the patties and gravy over the potatoes.

name: Sloppy Joe Rice Bowls
ingredients: Olive Oil: 2 tsp (beef) + oil for base (20 g)
Apple Cider Vinegar (Great Value): 1 tbsp (30 g)
steps: Brown 5.4 pounds of 93/7 ground beef with the chopped onion and green bell peppers, then drain.
Stir in the tomato sauce, tomato paste, ketchup, dijon, and garlic.
Simmer until the sauce thickens and clings to the meat.
Cook the rice separately so it stays fluffy.
Spoon the sloppy joe beef over the rice in each container.

name: Slow Cooker Apple Cider Pork Bowls
ingredients: Honey Dijon Mustard (Great Value): 1 bottle (60 g)
steps: Cut the pork loin into big chunks and lay them in the slow cooker.
Add the sliced apples and onions right on top.
Stir the honey dijon mustard, onion powder, and garlic powder together, then pour it over everything.
Cover and cook on low for 7 to 8 hours until the pork shreds with a fork.
While that finishes, roast or boil the potatoes until fork tender.
Pull the pork, spoon it over the potatoes, and ladle a little of that cider gravy over the top.

Steam the green beans until crisp-tender and set aside.
Shred the pork and stir it back through the balsamic glaze.
Divide the pork, potatoes, and green beans into your containers.

name: Slow Cooker Barbacoa Burrito Bowl
ingredients: Chipotle in Adobo (La Costena): 1 can (105 g)
Seasoned Black Beans (Great Value): 4 cans (910 g)
Fat Free Cheddar (Great Value): 1 bag (196 g)
Apple Cider Vinegar (Great Value): 2 tbsp (60 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot on a kitchen scale and write the number down. You will need it to portion evenly at the end.
Cut the chuck roast into big 3 inch chunks and drop them in the slow cooker.

Add the diced yellow onion, minced garlic, a few finely chopped chipotle peppers with a spoonful of their adobo sauce, the lime juice, cumin, a pinch of salt and pepper, and the beef broth. Stir it all together with tongs.
Cover and cook on low for 8 to 9 hours or on high for 4 to 5 hours, until the beef falls apart when you poke it with a fork.
Lift the beef onto a cutting board and shred it with two forks. Skim the fat off the top of the cooking liquid and pour some of the broth back over the meat so it stays juicy.
Cook your rice per the package. Warm and drain the black beans.
To build the bowls, layer rice on the bottom, then a scoop of barbacoa, then beans, and finish with a sprinkle of fat free cheddar.

name: Slow Cooker BBQ Pulled Chicken Bowls
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast (Member's Mark): 8 lb (3300 g)
BBQ Sauce (Sugar Free) (Sweet Baby Ray's): 1 bottle (500 g)
Sweet Whole Kernel Corn (Great Value): 3 cans (750 g)
steps: Lay the chicken breasts in the bottom of the slow cooker.
Sprinkle the paprika and garlic powder over the top, then pour on the BBQ sauce.
Cover and cook on low for 7 to 8 hours until the chicken shreds with a fork.
Shred the chicken right in the pot and stir it back through the sauce.
Warm the corn and fold it in, or spoon it over the top.
Serve over cooked white rice and portion into your containers.

name: Slow Cooker Buffalo Chicken and Rice Bowl
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast (Member's Mark): 6 lb (2495 g)
Ranch Seasoning Mix (Hidden Valley): 1 packet (47 g)
Buffalo Wing Sauce (Frank's RedHot): 1 bottle (240 g)
Fat Free Cheddar (Great Value): 1 bag (196 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot on a kitchen scale and write the number down. You will need it to portion evenly at the end.

Put the chicken breast in the slow cooker, sprinkle on the ranch seasoning, and pour over the buffalo sauce. Cook on low for 6 to 8 hours or high for 3 to 4, until the chicken pulls apart with a fork.
While that finishes, cook your rice per the package. This is your base and it stretches the whole batch.
Roast or steam the broccoli florets until just tender and still bright green. Do not overcook it or it turns to mush by day three.
Shred the chicken while it is still warm, right in the slow cooker, using two forks. Warm chicken shreds far easier than cold.
Toss the shredded chicken back through its own cooking liquid so every bite stays juicy and coated.
Add the cooked rice, broccoli, and the shredded cheddar to your weighed mixing pot and fold everything together.

Shred the chicken, then stir in the milk and Greek yogurt for that creamy finish.

Spoon the butter chicken over rice and serve.

ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast (Member's Mark): 8 lb (3450 g)
